subject.title: Durable Core PR 6/6: add read-only durable inspection

question: Should OpenClaw adopt a new opt-in, cross-owner durable-runtime core—with persistent state, durable.mode configuration, recovery-worker behavior, and public durable Gateway/CLI APIs—or keep these concerns within existing owner-specific lifecycles?
rationale: The patch is a broad architectural and product-contract addition spanning storage, agent ingress, restart recovery, session delivery, CLI behavior, and Gateway protocol; implementation review cannot safely choose that boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: Defer shared durable core
options.body: Do not merge the cumulative stack now; require future narrow owner-specific repairs unless a maintainer identifies an irreducible shared-core gap.

options.title: Sponsor a bounded core contract
options.body: Accept the direction with named owners for storage, recovery, upgrade behavior, and the public durable Gateway/CLI contract before staged landing.

options.title: Request a narrower proposal
options.body: Ask for a reduced implementation that proves one cross-owner gap cannot be handled by existing lifecycle owners.

recommendation.title: Defer shared durable core
recommendation.body: Do not merge the cumulative stack now; require future narrow owner-specific repairs unless a maintainer identifies an irreducible shared-core gap.

likelyOwner.reason: mjnkao authored the proposal series and is the available routing contact for clarifying its intended boundaries; maintainer sponsorship itself remains unassigned.
